title: Age-predicted maximal heart rate revisited
publisher: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
claims: A meta-analysis collected group mean maximal heart rate values from 351 studies involving 492 groups and 18,712 subjects.
Maximal heart rate was strongly related to age (r = -0.90), with the regression equation 208 - 0.7 × age.
A laboratory-based cross-validation in 514 healthy subjects produced 209 - 0.7 × age, virtually identical to the meta-analysis equation.
The regression line was not different between men and women and was not influenced by wide variations in habitual physical activity.
The older 220 - age equation underestimates maximal heart rate in older adults.
The authors recommend 208 - 0.7 × age as a regression equation to predict maximal heart rate in healthy adults.
